conversation_lines.speaker: Doctor
conversation_lines.text: Hi, I’m Dr. Lee. I’ll be your doctor during this stay. You’re here because of nausea and vomiting—can you tell me what happened today?

conversation_lines.speaker: Patient
conversation_lines.text: Yes, I woke up feeling fine, but right before my big work presentation, I suddenly felt nauseous and started vomiting. I’ve thrown up several times already, all watery, no blood.

conversation_lines.speaker: Doctor
conversation_lines.text: I see. Any fever, abdominal pain, or diarrhea?

conversation_lines.speaker: Patient
conversation_lines.text: No, none of that. It feels just like my past episodes—probably my gastroparesis flaring up again.

conversation_lines.speaker: Doctor
conversation_lines.text: That makes sense. You have type 1 diabetes and a gastric pacer, right?

conversation_lines.speaker: Patient
conversation_lines.text: Yes, and I’ve had this happen many times before—especially when I’m anxious.

conversation_lines.speaker: Doctor
conversation_lines.text: Exactly. The vomiting likely started because of anxiety, which triggered your gastroparesis. We’ll give you IV fluids and anti-nausea meds to help.

conversation_lines.speaker: Patient
conversation_lines.text: Okay, that sounds good. I haven’t eaten since yesterday—just couldn’t keep anything down.

conversation_lines.speaker: Doctor
conversation_lines.text: We’ll keep you NPO for now—nothing by mouth—until the vomiting stops. You already got Zofran, Compazine, and Ativan in the ER. How are you feeling now?

conversation_lines.speaker: Patient
conversation_lines.text: A little calmer, but still nauseous. The Ativan helped with the anxiety a bit.

conversation_lines.speaker: Doctor
conversation_lines.text: Good. We’ll keep monitoring. Your blood sugar was 73 when you arrived—low but not dangerous. We gave insulin and will adjust as needed.

conversation_lines.speaker: Patient
conversation_lines.text: I usually take glargine at night. Should I still take it?

conversation_lines.speaker: Doctor
conversation_lines.text: Yes, we’ll continue your usual 28 units of glargine tonight. We’re also giving sliding scale insulin as needed.

conversation_lines.speaker: Patient
conversation_lines.text: Okay, thanks. My blood pressure has been high during these episodes too.

conversation_lines.speaker: Doctor
conversation_lines.text: Yes, your BP was elevated—158/94. That’s considered hypertensive urgency, especially since you couldn’t take your lisinopril today. We’ll restart it once you can keep fluids down.

conversation_lines.speaker: Patient
conversation_lines.text: I only take lisinopril 20 mg daily. I’ve never taken metoprolol—I saw it on a past note and got confused.

conversation_lines.speaker: Doctor
conversation_lines.text: Noted. We’ll stick with lisinopril. Your PCP will check your BP after discharge and may adjust the dose if needed.

conversation_lines.speaker: Doctor
conversation_lines.text: Good morning. You made it through the night without vomiting. That’s a great sign. Your labs this morning show mild anemia—your hemoglobin dropped from 12.1 to 10.3—but no other major issues.

conversation_lines.speaker: Patient
conversation_lines.text: Is that from the vomiting? I’ve had iron deficiency before.

conversation_lines.speaker: Doctor
conversation_lines.text: Likely chronic, not acute. We’re not concerned about bleeding—no blood in vomit or stool. We’ll continue monitoring, but no transfusion needed.

conversation_lines.speaker: Patient
conversation_lines.text: Okay, that’s a relief. Can I try drinking something now?

conversation_lines.speaker: Doctor
conversation_lines.text: Yes, we’ll start with small sips of water. If you keep that down, we’ll advance to clear liquids, then soft foods.

conversation_lines.speaker: Patient
conversation_lines.text: And my Reglan? I usually take that three times a day.

conversation_lines.speaker: Doctor
conversation_lines.text: We’ll restart Reglan once you’re on oral meds. It helps with stomach emptying. We’re also continuing your amitriptyline and citalopram for nerve pain and mood.

conversation_lines.speaker: Doctor
conversation_lines.text: You’ve kept down water and broth—great job. We’re upgrading you to a soft diet. How’s your nausea?

conversation_lines.speaker: Patient
conversation_lines.text: Much better. Still a little anxious, but not nauseous.

conversation_lines.speaker: Doctor
conversation_lines.text: You can take your Ativan 0.5 mg as needed for anxiety. We’re also restarting lisinopril and Reglan by mouth.

conversation_lines.speaker: Patient
conversation_lines.text: Should I take Ativan before stressful events to prevent this?

conversation_lines.speaker: Doctor
conversation_lines.text: Yes, that’s a good idea. The discharge instructions say to take Ativan if you feel anxious and start to feel nauseous—it might stop the cycle.

conversation_lines.speaker: Doctor
conversation_lines.text: You’ve had two meals without vomiting—excellent progress. Your blood sugar this morning was 260, a bit high, but expected since you’re not eating normally.

conversation_lines.speaker: Patient
conversation_lines.text: I’ll adjust my insulin once I’m back on a regular schedule. No signs of ketoacidosis, right?

conversation_lines.speaker: Doctor
conversation_lines.text: Correct. No ketones, no acidosis. Your sodium is slightly low at 132, but that’s common with vomiting and IV fluids. It should normalize.

conversation_lines.speaker: Patient
conversation_lines.text: I’m glad it’s not DKA. I’ve been scared of that since I was young.

conversation_lines.speaker: Doctor
conversation_lines.text: We’re watching closely. You’re stable now. Planning to discharge you tomorrow morning if you keep doing well.

conversation_lines.speaker: Patient
conversation_lines.text: I feel ready to go home. What’s the plan for follow-up?

conversation_lines.speaker: Doctor
conversation_lines.text: You’ll see your GI doctor tomorrow to discuss your gastric pacer and ongoing gastroparesis. And your PCP next week to check your blood pressure and review lisinopril.

conversation_lines.speaker: Doctor
conversation_lines.text: You’ve had a full night without symptoms. We’ll discharge you home today. All your meds are back to baseline—no changes.

conversation_lines.speaker: Patient
conversation_lines.text: So same doses: glargine 28 units, lisinopril 20 mg, Reglan, citalopram, amitriptyline, and Ativan as needed?

conversation_lines.speaker: Doctor
conversation_lines.text: Exactly. Take Ativan if anxiety starts—might prevent another episode. And call your team if vomiting returns.

conversation_lines.speaker: Patient
conversation_lines.text: Thank you. I’ll try to manage stress better and follow up as planned.

conversation_lines.speaker: Doctor
conversation_lines.text: You did great. Stay hydrated, eat small meals, and reach out if you need help. Safe travels home.
